Rashi on Ketubot 53a:10:1.hebrew: ואמר רב פפא כתובת בנין דכרין - והכי קאמר: מתה היא בחיי שניהם וירשוה הם, אין בנים שיש לה מזה ומזה נוטלין כתובת אמן כבנין דכרין כשבאין לחלוק בנכסי אביהם, אלא חולקין בשוה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:10:1.english: And Rav Pappa said: The ketubah of male children - And this is what he is saying: [If] she died during the lifetime of both of them and they inherited her, the sons whom she has from this [husband] and from that [husband] do not take their mother's ketubah [under the stipulation of] "male children" when they come to divide their father's property; rather, they divide [it] equally.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:10:2.hebrew: ואמאי - כיון דאמרינן כי אניסא, לא מפסדא כתובת בנין דכרין:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:10:2.english: And why - Since we say [that] when she is forced, she does not forfeit the ketubbah of male children.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:10:3.english: Let us say desire forced her - For she desired a husband.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:11:1.english: A penalty - Because she did not investigate thoroughly that her husband had died before she married.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:12:1.hebrew: אין לה מזונות - באלמנותה, דתנאי כתובה ככתובה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:12:1.english: She has no sustenance - during her widowhood, for a stipulation of the ketubah is like the ketubah [itself].

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:1.hebrew: או הב לה כתובה - דתקנו קבורתה תחת כתובתה, וסבר למימר תחת מנה מאתים שתקנו לה חכמים:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:1.english: Or give her [her] marriage contract - For [the Sages] instituted her burial in place of her marriage contract, and [he] thought to say [that this means] in place of the maneh [or] two hundred [zuz] that the Sages instituted for her.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:2.hebrew: תנינא - אני שונה שאין לארוסה שמתה משפט כתובה, דהיינו קבורה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:2.english: We learned - I teach [a baraita] that a betrothed woman who died does not have the law of a ketubah, namely, burial.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:3.english: [He is] not an acute mourner - to be forbidden from [eating] sacrificial food.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:4.hebrew: ולא מיטמא לה - אם כהן הוא, דלאו שארו היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:4.english: Nor does he become ritually impure for her - [That is,] if he is a priest, for she is not his relative.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:5.hebrew: ולא מיטמאה לו - אינה חייבת ליטמא לו. ואע"פ שמצוה להתעסק בששה מתי מצוה האמורים בפרשת כהנים (ויקרא כא), דכתיב "לה יטמא", מצוה זו אינה מהם, דלאו שארו היא. אבל אם רוצה היא ליטמא, אינה מוזהרת מליטמא, אפילו כהנת, ד"בני אהרן" כתיב, ולא בנות אהרן:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:5.english: Nor does she become ritually impure for him - She is not obligated to become ritually impure for him. And even though it is a mitzvah to attend to the six relatives [for whom becoming impure is] a mitzvah that are stated in the section of the priests (Leviticus 21), as it is written, "for her he shall become impure," this mitzvah is not among them, for she is not his close relative [she'ero]. However, if she wishes to become ritually impure, she is not prohibited from becoming ritually impure, even [if she is] the daughter of a priest, for "the sons of Aaron" is written, and not the daughters of Aaron.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:6.hebrew: אינו יורשה - נדוניית בית אביה, דלא תקון ירושת הבעל עד שתכנס לחופה או שתמסר לשלוחים:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:6.english: He does not inherit her - [i.e.,] the dowry of her father's house, for [the Sages] did not institute a husband's inheritance until she enters the bridal canopy or is handed over to [his] agents.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:7.english: [If] he died - during her lifetime.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:13:8.english: She collects her marriage contract - A maneh [or] two hundred [zuz], and the additional amount if he wrote [it] for her.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:14:1.hebrew: אין לה כתובה - דין כתובה, וקבורתה תחת כתובתה דתניא לעיל — בנשואה תניא, ותחת נדוניית בית אביה שהוא יורשה. אבל הכא, כיון דכי מתה אינו יורשה, אף הוא לא נתחייב לקוברה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:14:1.english: She does not have a marriage contract - [That is, the] law of a marriage contract; and [as for] her burial [being] in place of her marriage contract, which was taught earlier, [that] was taught with regard to a married woman, and [it is] in exchange for the dowry of her father's house, which he inherits from her. However, here, since when she dies he does not inherit her, he is also not obligated to bury her.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:14:2.hebrew: מאי טעמא - דאמרינן כי מתה בחייו אין לה תביעת כתובה, תקבר בשביל מנה מאתים שהוא יורש:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:14:2.english: What is the reason - that we say when she dies in his lifetime she has no claim to a marriage contract? Let her be buried on account of the maneh [or] two hundred [zuz] that he inherits!

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:14:3.hebrew: שאין אני קורא כו' - וכך היו כותבין בשטר כתובתה. הלכך, כל זמן שלא מת ולא נתגרשה, לא נשתעבד לה, ולא יורש ממנה כלום:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:14:3.english: For I do not read, etc. - And thus they would write in her ketubah document. Therefore, as long as he has not died and she has not been divorced, he has not become obligated to her, and [her heir] does not inherit anything from her.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:1:1.english: He saw - Rav Pappa [saw] that Yehuda was not amenable to enter.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:1:2.hebrew: וכ"ש מברא לברתא - והכא איעבורי אחסנתא הוא, שזה כותב לבתו מה שהיה ראוי להוריש לבניו:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:1:2.english: And all the more so from a son to a daughter - And here it is a transfer of inheritance, for this [man] is writing to his daughter that which was fitting to bequeath to his sons.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:2:1.hebrew: דא"ר יוחנן - לעיל, שיקפוץ אדם ויתן לבתו, ויליף לה מקרא:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:2:1.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said - Above, that a person should hasten and give [a dowry] to his daughter, and he derives it from a verse.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:2:2.english: To force him as well - [This is asked] as a question.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:2:3.hebrew: מעלאי דידי היינו עשויי - כניסתי עמך זהו עשוי, שירבה לפסוק בשביל כבודי:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:2:3.english: My own entrance is forcing [him] - My entering with you, this is forcing [him], for he will pledge more on account of my honor.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:3:1.hebrew: אכפייה - רב פפא ליהודה בדברים, ועל:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:3:1.english: He pressed him - Rav Pappa [pressed] Yehuda with words, and he entered.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:3:2.hebrew: סבר איהו - אבא סוראה, האי דשתיק יהודה מרתח רתח, שאין הנדוניא הוגנת בעיניו:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:3:2.english: He thought - Abba of Sura [thought that] the reason Yehuda was silent [was that] he was angry, because the dowry was not fitting in his eyes.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:4:1.english: If [it were] from me - If you had taken advice from me.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:5:1.hebrew: או אין לה - מי אמרינן, כיון דמכרה לבעלה, פקעה לה תורת ירושת אביה מלהוריש נדוניא שלו לבני בתו — שהרי מכרתה, ואין כל הירושה באה מעכשיו אלא מכח הבעל — ויחלקו כל בניו בשוה, בני ב' נשיו:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:5:1.english: Or does she not have [it] - Do we say [that] since she sold [her marriage contract] to her husband, the law of her father's inheritance has lapsed from bequeathing his dowry to his daughter's sons — for she has sold it, and the entire inheritance now comes only by virtue of the husband — and [therefore] all of his sons, the sons of his two wives, shall divide [it] equally?

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:5:2.hebrew: ותיבעי לך מוחלת - שהוא דבר מצוי מן המכר, ואי משום דלא מטא הנאה לידה, מכל מקום פקעה זכותה בחייה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:5:2.english: And you can raise the dilemma [regarding] one who forgoes - For that is a more common occurrence than selling; and if [you distinguish between them] because no benefit reached her hand, nevertheless, her right expired during her lifetime.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:6:1.hebrew: השתא מוכרת מבעיא לי - כלומר, מי סברת דמשום הנאה דמטא לידה תיסק אדעתאי דפקעה זכותה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:6:1.english: Now, one who sells is a dilemma for me - That is to say, do you think that [it is] because of the benefit that came into her hand [that] it would enter my mind that her right was voided?

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:6:2.hebrew: השתא מוכרת - דאנוסה היא, סלקא אדעתאי דפקעה זכותה ומיבעיא לי, כל שכן מוחלת דלא אנוסה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:6:2.english: Now, one who sells - [Even though] she is under duress, it enters my mind that her right lapses and it is a dilemma for me; all the more so one who forgoes [it], who is not under duress.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:6:3.hebrew: מחו לה מאה עוכלי בעוכלא - מכין אותה מאה מכות ברצועה שבראשה ברזל, כמין משקולת קטנה ששמה עוכלא:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:6:3.english: They strike her a hundred uklei with an ukla - They strike her a hundred blows with a strap that has iron at its head, like a small weight called ukla.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:7:1.hebrew: מוכרת כתובתה לאחרים - בטובת הנאה, שאם נתארמלה או נתגרשה יטלוה לקוחות, ואם מתה ירשנה בעלה. ומתה וירשה בעלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:7:1.english: One who sells her marriage contract to others - For a nominal benefit, [meaning] that if she is widowed or divorced, the buyers will take it, and if she dies, her husband will inherit her. And [in this case] she died and her husband inherited her.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:7:2.hebrew: יש לבניה כתובת בנין דכרין - דהא כי לא זבינתה נמי ירית לה בעל, ותקון לה רבנן. השתא נמי לגבי בעל, במוכרת לא פקעה זכותה. ואי משום דהוקל בעיניה למוכרה ולהפסיד את בניה אם נתארמלה או נתגרשה, זוזי אנסוה שהוצרכה להם:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:7:2.english: Her sons have the marriage contract [stipulation] of male children - For even when she did not sell it, the husband inherits it, yet the Rabbis instituted [this stipulation] for her. Now too, with respect to the husband, when she sells [it], her right is not forfeited. And if [one argues] that she treated it lightly by selling it and causing her sons to lose [it] should she be widowed or divorced — money forced her, for she needed it.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:7:3.english: She has indeed forgiven it - And it is a light matter in her eyes to deprive her sons of her ketubah for nothing.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:8:1.hebrew: מוכרת לבעלה - נמי טובת הנאה בעלמא, דבר מועט, שהרי אם מתה יורשה, ואינו לוקח ממנה אלא שאם מת הוא לא תגבה. והרי לא מת ובא לידי ירושה, הלכך כמוכרת לאחרים דמי:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:8:1.english: One who sells [her marriage contract] to her husband - [This is] also merely a contingent benefit, a small amount, for if she dies, he inherits her, and he is only purchasing from her that if he dies, she will not collect [it]. And behold, he did not die, and it came to inheritance; therefore, she is considered like one who sells to others.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:8:2.english: Or is she considered like one who forgoes [her marriage contract] to her husband - Since the marriage contract is in his possession, and it was easy in her eyes to relinquish it permanently.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:9:1.hebrew: אין יורשין של זה כו' - משנה היא ביבמות: האשה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים, ואמר לה עד אחד "מת בעליך", והתירוה לינשא, ונישאת, ואחר כך בא בעלה — תצא מזה ומזה, ואין לה כתובה לא מזה ולא מזה; ואם מתה, אין יורשין של זה וזה — בנים שיש לה מזה ומזה — יורשין כתובתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 53a:9:1.english: Neither the heirs of this [one], etc. - It is a Mishnah in Yevamot: A woman whose husband went overseas, and one witness said to her, "Your husband died," and they permitted her to marry, and she married, and afterward her husband came [back] — she must leave both this [one] and that [one], and she has no marriage contract from either this [one] or that [one]; and if she died, neither the heirs of this [one] nor [of] that [one] — [namely,] the sons whom she has from this [one] and from that [one] — inherit her marriage contract.

Rashi on Ketubot 53a:9:2.english: And we discussed it: What is [the purpose of] her marriage contract - Behold, you said she has no marriage contract.

Tosafot on Ketubot 53a:14:1.hebrew: שאין אני קורא בה לכשתנשאי לאחר תטלי מה שכתוב ליכי - והא דתניא לעיל (כתובות דף מז:): "קבורתה תחת כתובתה" — היינו נדוניית כתובתה, והיינו דוקא נשואה שהוא יורש נדונייתה; ומצינו שנקראת נדוניא "כתובה", כדאמר לעיל (כתובות דף מח:): "נכנסה עמו ללון, אע"פ שכתובתה בבית בעלה". ואם תאמר: והא מדרש כתובה לא דרשי אלא בית שמאי, כדאמרינן בפרק האשה שלום (יבמות דף קטז: ושם), דתנן: "האשה שאמרה מת בעלי — ב"ש אומרים: תנשא ותטול כתובה, וב"ה אומרים: תנשא ולא תטול כתובה" כו'; א"ל ב"ש לב"ה: "והלא מספר כתובה נלמד, שהרי כותב לה: 'לכשתנשאי לאחר' כו'". ואע"ג דקתני התם: "חזרו ב"ה להורות כב"ש" — לא משום דאית להו מדרש כתובה הדרי בהו, אלא מק"ו שאמרו להו ב"ש: "התרתם הערוה החמורה, לא נתיר ממון הקל?". דהא אמר בפרק האשה שנפלו (לקמן כתובות דף פא. ושם): "מאן שמעת להו דאית להו מדרש כתובה? ב"ש", משמע דלא חזרו ב"ה משום מדרש כתובה, אלא מק"ו כדפרי'. וא"כ, היכי אתי הכא כב"ש? ותו: אביי ורבא דדרשי לעיל (כתובות דף נא.): "ואהדרינך למדינתך ואותבינך לאינתו", ושמואל דדריש נמי לשון השטר בפ"ק דב"מ (דף טו.) גבי הא דאמר: "בעל חוב גובה את השבח; תדע, שכך כותב לו: 'ואנא איקום ואישפי' כו'" — אטו כולהו כב"ש? והא בית שמאי במקום בית הלל אינה משנה! ונראה דבהא הלכה כב"ש, משום דאשכחנא כמה תנאי דקיימי כוותיה בריש המקבל (ב"מ דף קד. ושם) דדרשי לשון הדיוט: רבי מאיר, ורבי יהודה, והלל הזקן, ורבי יהושע בן קרחה, ורבי יוסי. וכיון דדרשי לשון הדיוט, שנהגו ההדיוטות לכתוב בשטרות אע"פ שלא תקנו חכמים — כ"ש תנאי כתובה שהוא תקון חכמים; והתם בהמקבל (ג"ז שם) מוכח דהכי הלכתא. ומיהו קשה מבית הלל אהלל הזקן! ושמא אע"ג דבית הלל הם תלמידי הלל הזקן, פליגי עליה. אי נמי: כי לית להו לבית הלל מדרש כתובה — היינו לגרע כחה, אבל לייפות כחה אית להו. ולהכי חזרו בית הלל להודות לבית שמאי ביבמות, דהתם הוי ליפות כחה — ולא משום קל וחומר דהתם, כדמוכח מתניתין דהתם. וההיא דהמקבל נמי לייפות כחה, דעל ידי שהיה כתוב בכתובת אמן: "לכשתכנסי לחופה הוי לי לאינתו", לא עשה בניה ממזרים, ובתר חזרה אמרה הלל הזקן. ומיהו בית שמאי אית להו מדרש כתובה אפילו לגרע כחה, וקיימא לן כוותייהו, דהא הכא בשמעתין לגרע כחה הוא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 53a:14:1.english: "Because I do not read with regard to her: 'When you marry another, you shall take what is written for you'" - And that which was taught in a baraita earlier (Ketubot 47b): "[The obligation of] her burial is in place of her ketubah" — that refers to the dowry [written in] her ketubah, and that applies specifically to a married woman, since he inherits her dowry; and we find that a dowry is called "ketubah," as it states earlier (Ketubot 48b): "[If] she entered with him to lodge [for the night], even though her ketubah is in her husband's house." And if you will say: But [the principle of] expounding the text of a ketubah (midrash ketubah) is only expounded by Beit Shammai, as we say in the chapter HaIshah Shalom (Yevamot 116b and there [in Tosafot]), where we learned in a Mishnah: "A woman who said, 'My husband died' — Beit Shammai say: She may marry and collect her ketubah, and Beit Hillel say: She may marry, but she may not collect her ketubah," etc. Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel: "Is it not learned from the text of the ketubah, for he writes to her: 'When you marry another,'" etc.? And even though it teaches there: "Beit Hillel retracted to rule in accordance with Beit Shammai," they did not retract because they hold of expounding the ketubah, but rather because of an a fortiori argument (kal vachomer) that Beit Shammai said to them: "You have permitted the severe matter of forbidden sexual relations; shall we not permit the lenient matter of money?" For it says in the chapter HaIshah SheNaflu (below, Ketubot 81a and there): "Whom have you heard who holds of expounding the ketubah? Beit Shammai" — which implies that Beit Hillel did not retract because of expounding the ketubah, but rather because of the kal vachomer, as I have explained. And if so, how does [the Gemara] here accord with Beit Shammai? And furthermore: Abaye and Rava, who expound earlier (Ketubot 51a) [the clause]: "And I will return you to your province and take you back as a wife"; and Shmuel, who also expounds the wording of a document in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (15a) regarding that which he said: "A creditor collects the appreciation [of the property]; know [that this is so], for thus he writes to him: 'And I will stand and clear [it],'" etc. — do all of these follow Beit Shammai?! Surely [a ruling of] Beit Shammai in opposition to Beit Hillel is not authoritative! And it appears [to Tosafot] that in this matter the halakhah follows Beit Shammai, because we find several Tannaim who stand in accordance with him at the beginning of [the chapter] HaMekabbel (Bava Metzia 104a and there) who expound commoners' wording: Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehudah, Hillel the Elder, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah, and Rabbi Yose. And since they expound commoners' wording — which ordinary people are accustomed to write in documents even though the Sages did not institute it — all the more so [do we expound] a ketubah stipulation, which is an enactment of the Sages! And there in HaMekabbel (also there) it is proven that such is the halakhah. However, there is a difficulty from Beit Hillel against Hillel the Elder! Perhaps even though Beit Hillel are the disciples of Hillel the Elder, they disagree with him. Alternatively: When Beit Hillel do not hold of expounding the ketubah, that is [only] to diminish her power [i.e., to her detriment], but to strengthen her power [i.e., to her benefit], they do hold of it. And for this reason Beit Hillel retracted to concede to Beit Shammai in Yevamot, for there it was to strengthen her power — and not because of the kal vachomer there, as is evident from the Mishnah there. And that case in HaMekabbel was also to strengthen her power, for because it was written in their mothers' ketubah, "When you enter the marriage canopy, be a wife to me," he did not render her children mamzerim; and Hillel the Elder stated this after the retraction. However, Beit Shammai hold of expounding the ketubah even to diminish her power, and we rule in accordance with them, for here in our sugya it is to diminish her power.

Tosafot on Ketubot 53a:4:1.hebrew: השתא נמי אהדר בי - אע"ג דהן הן דברים הנקנים באמירה, היינו היכא דעמדו וקדשו, והכא כשרצה לחזור עדיין לא קדשו. אי נמי, הכא כבר קידשו [קודם] לכן ואח"כ כתב, ולא אמרינן הן הן דברים הנקנים באמירה אלא כשקידשו אחר כך:
Tosafot on Ketubot 53a:4:1.english: Now too, I will retract - Even though these are matters that are acquired through speech, that applies [only] where they arose and betrothed, whereas here, when he wanted to retract, they had not yet betrothed. Alternatively, here they had already betrothed prior to this and afterwards he wrote [the document], and we do not say "these are matters acquired through speech" except when they betrothed afterwards.

Tosafot on Ketubot 53a:5:1.hebrew: ותבעי לך מוחלת - נראה לר"י לפרש דהוה לך למנקט בעייתך במוחלת, דשכיח טפי, כדפירש בקונטרס. ומסיק: השתא מוכרת, דאיכא למימר זוזי אנסוה, אפ"ה דעתי נוטה לומר הואיל ומכרה הפסידה — מוחלת מיבעיא?! דפשיטא דלית לה כתובת בנין דכרין. וכה"ג פר"ח בשילהי המצניע (שבת דף צה:) גבי ניקב בכדי טהרתו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 53a:5:1.english: And you can raise [the dilemma regarding] one who forgoes - It appears to Ri [that this is] to be explained [as meaning]: You should have framed your dilemma with respect to one who forgoes [her marriage contract], which is more common, as Rashi explained. And [Rav Yeimar] concludes: Now, [even in the case of] one who sells [her marriage contract], where one could say [that] the money forced her, even so my mind inclines to say [that] since she sold it, she has forfeited [her right] — is there any question [regarding] one who forgoes [it]?! For it is obvious that she does not have the marriage document concerning male children. And similarly, Rabbeinu Chananel explained at the end of [the chapter entitled] Hamatzni'a (Shabbat 95b) regarding [a vessel that] was perforated to the extent of its purification.
